# Was the Steam outage a cyberattack?

**Not established.** No source we read says either Steam disruption was an attack, and none rules one out. Valve has not given a cause. A spike in user reports does not show an attack.

Incident: Steam outages, Nov 17 and Nov 20-21, 2026. Also reported as the Steam outage, Steam down and Valve Steam outage. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 3:12 AM ET.

Picture: A Steam Deck OLED showing the Steam home screen (cropped). Image: SparklesTrainNerd, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Steam_Deck_OLED_framsida_hemsk%C3%A4rm.jpg).

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Valve, Steam, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 3:12 AM ET: **Valve has not said what caused Steam's Nov 17 outage or the Nov 20-21 problems. Nobody has reported a hack.** First draft. 6 sources (1 Tier 1, 4 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 13 claims (2 Confirmed, 8 Reported, 3 Not established), 6 questions. The Nov 17 outage is Confirmed by XDA's first-hand check, IT Home and an independent tracker. Whether either disruption was a cyberattack is Not established: no cause, no claim, no statement either way, and tracker spikes are not evidence of an attack. The Nov 20-21 reports rest on user-report trackers relayed by two outlets; Valve had not commented. We found no DDoS claim to carry as a rumor. Privacy check done: no names of private people, no handles, no contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. Steam is the largest PC game store, and the Nov 17 outage drew tens of thousands of user reports and took down downloads, the Store and cloud saves. The later reports are in the low thousands. Valve has not said how many people were affected.
- Who is affected: Steam users on Tuesday evening, Nov 17, who could not download, use Friends or load the Store, and users who reported sign-in, connection or checkout problems from late Friday, Nov 20, into Saturday, Nov 21. The Tuesday outage appears fixed; the later reports looked ongoing.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 30,000+ | Downdetector reports, Nov 17 | Near 48,000 at one point, per XDA |
| 1,600+ | Reports in an hour, Nov 20-21 | Tracker figure from about 11:47 PM ET, per IBTimes AU |

### Known so far

- Steam had a broad outage on Tuesday evening, Nov 17, that took down downloads, Friends, cloud saves and the Store for many users.
- The White House said on Nov 18 that it sees no indication of a cyberattack behind recent tech outages. It does not name Steam.

### Not known yet

- What caused either disruption. Valve has not said.
- Whether it was a cyberattack. No one has claimed one, reported one, or ruled one out.
- Whether the Nov 17 and Nov 20-21 problems are connected.
- How many people were affected.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of the time of this page's first draft.

- A Valve or Steam statement, status page or post giving the cause of either disruption.
- A Valve notice that the Nov 17 outage was planned maintenance.
- Any claim of responsibility, DDoS claim or credible report of a hack.
- A count of affected users.
- Any official statement tying the Steam disruptions to other outages. The White House's Nov 18 statement does not name Steam.
- Downdetector, IsItDownRightNow and StatusGator pages themselves. We relied on how news outlets relay them. We read Instatus's page for Nov 17 but do not quote its report counts, which changed between two loads.
- Steam's own social posts. We did not look at social media.
